learningObjective: Reason about the trade-off between W4A16 group size, quantization accuracy, and metadata bandwidth.

canonicalClaims.claim: In W4A16 quantization with FP16 scales, smaller group sizes give one scale per fewer weights → tighter distribution fit and higher accuracy, but proportionally more metadata; group_size 128 is a common default balancing accuracy and ~3% metadata overhead.
nonImplications: Does not imply group=32 is always best; kernel-side handling of many scales can add latency.
Does not imply the trade-off is identical across all models.

misconceptions.claim: Group size has no meaningful effect on accuracy; observed perplexity differences are noise.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Group size directly controls scale-factor granularity and has a systematic, well-documented effect on quantization accuracy.

misconceptions.claim: Smaller groups are always better because more scales mean more information.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Metadata overhead grows inversely with group size; at group=1 (per-weight) the metadata equals the weight size, defeating quantization.

misconceptions.claim: Metadata cost is negligible and never affects wall-clock decode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For very small groups, metadata bandwidth is meaningful; the kernel must load both weights and scales.

misconceptions.claim: Group size only affects offline quantization time; runtime is unaffected.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Runtime kernels must load and broadcast scale metadata; smaller groups mean more scale loads per weight.

implementationFacts: Marlin kernel supports group_size 128 with efficient scale broadcast.
performanceScenarios: For LLaMA-7B, group=128 with AWQ recovers within 0.2 perplexity of FP16; group=32 recovers within 0.1 but with higher metadata cost.
